title: Taking Frankie Rekuparo to the colored theater with charcoal on his face
summary: A story of his Italian friend Frankie, whose father had a grocery, and the stunt of blackening Frankie's face to get into a Tom Mix movie at the Star Theater.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: And these kids and I would play together all the time. And one of these kinds, Frankie Rekuparo, we were such close friends as kids until he wanted to go to theater with me, and that was kind of taboo down South in those days. And Frankie -- we were kids, just young kids. And I worked for his father's grocery store delivering groceries. But they would help me deliver the groceries.

By anyway, one day I took Frankie and I put some charcoal dust all over his face -- I never forgot this when he was a little kid -- because he wanted to see a movie that was at the colored theater, the Star Theater at West Broad Street. And this was a picture with Tom Mix in it. I never forgot that. We loved cowboys, you know, in those days.
And so, he wanted to see this movie, and I put this charcoal dust all over his face, and on his hands. But I didn't put any on his neck and his legs. I took him to this

theater, and this old colored fellow -- gentleman -- nice guy. He smiled and he looked at us, and he let us in. I often think about what a bunch of nuts we were at that time. And this was a true story. I never forgot this, you know.
But we thought -- today I look back at it. I see this guy was so wise but he just didn't want to turn us down. He let us go in the theater, you know.
